title: Backend Developer role
content: Backend developers build server-side logic, REST APIs and databases. Common requirements: Python, Node.js or Java, SQL and NoSQL databases, REST API design, authentication and authorization, Git, Docker and automated testing. Junior roles value clean code and a portfolio of working API projects.

title: Frontend Developer role
content: Frontend developers build the user interface of web applications. Common requirements: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, a framework such as React, responsive design, accessibility, Git, consuming REST APIs and basic testing. A portfolio of deployed projects matters more than years of experience.

title: Full-Stack Developer role
content: Full-stack developers work on both frontend and backend. Common requirements: JavaScript or TypeScript, React, Node.js with Express or Python with FastAPI, MongoDB or SQL databases, REST APIs, Git and basic deployment knowledge.

title: Data Analyst role
content: Data analysts turn raw data into insights. Common requirements: SQL, Excel, Python with pandas, data visualization with Power BI or Tableau, basic statistics and clear communication of findings to non-technical people.

title: Machine Learning Engineer role
content: Machine learning engineers build, train and deploy models. Common requirements: Python, NumPy, pandas, scikit-learn, TensorFlow or PyTorch, model evaluation, SQL, linear algebra, probability and basic MLOps.

title: DevOps Engineer role
content: DevOps engineers automate building, testing and deploying software. Common requirements: Linux, Bash, Git, Docker, Kubernetes, CI/CD pipelines, a cloud provider such as AWS, monitoring and infrastructure as code.

title: Python
content: Python is a general-purpose language used for backend development, data analysis, automation and machine learning. Learn variables, functions, classes, virtual environments, error handling and popular libraries such as FastAPI, pandas and NumPy.

title: SQL
content: SQL is used to query relational databases. Learn SELECT, WHERE, JOIN, GROUP BY, subqueries, indexes and how to design tables with primary and foreign keys. SQL is required for backend, data analyst and many machine learning roles.

title: Git and GitHub
content: Git tracks code changes and GitHub hosts repositories. Learn commit, branch, merge, pull request and resolving conflicts. Recruiters check GitHub profiles, so keep clear README files and regular commits.

title: REST APIs
content: REST APIs let applications communicate over HTTP using methods such as GET, POST, PUT and DELETE, status codes and JSON. Learn resource naming, authentication with tokens, validation and clear error messages.

title: Docker
content: Docker packages an application with everything it needs into a container so it runs the same everywhere. Learn writing a Dockerfile, images, containers, volumes and docker-compose.

title: Soft skills
content: Employers value communication, teamwork, problem solving, time management, adaptability and willingness to learn. Show them with concrete examples such as leading a study group, volunteering, coaching others or delivering a team project.

title: Backend developer roadmap
content: 1) Learn Python or JavaScript. 2) Learn Git. 3) Learn SQL and one relational database. 4) Build REST APIs with FastAPI or Express. 5) Learn authentication and security basics. 6) Learn Docker and testing. 7) Deploy a project and build a portfolio.

title: Frontend developer roadmap
content: 1) Learn HTML and CSS. 2) Learn JavaScript deeply. 3) Learn Git. 4) Learn responsive design and accessibility. 5) Learn a framework such as React. 6) Consume REST APIs. 7) Build and deploy 3 to 5 portfolio projects.

title: Data analyst roadmap
content: 1) Learn Excel. 2) Learn SQL. 3) Learn statistics basics. 4) Learn Python with pandas. 5) Learn a visualization tool such as Power BI or Tableau. 6) Complete 3 portfolio analyses on public datasets. 7) Practice presenting insights.

title: Machine learning engineer roadmap
content: 1) Learn Python. 2) Learn math basics: linear algebra, probability, statistics. 3) Learn NumPy, pandas and scikit-learn. 4) Learn deep learning with PyTorch or TensorFlow. 5) Build projects and publish them. 6) Learn model deployment and MLOps basics.

title: DevOps engineer roadmap
content: 1) Learn Linux and Bash. 2) Learn Git. 3) Learn networking basics. 4) Learn Docker. 5) Learn CI/CD with GitHub Actions or GitLab CI. 6) Learn a cloud provider such as AWS. 7) Learn Kubernetes and infrastructure as code.

title: Web development learning resources
content: Free resources for web development: MDN Web Docs for HTML, CSS and JavaScript reference, freeCodeCamp for full courses, The Odin Project for a complete full-stack path and javascript.info for modern JavaScript.

title: Python and backend learning resources
content: Resources for Python and backend: the official Python tutorial, the official FastAPI tutorial in the FastAPI documentation, Real Python articles and Harvard CS50 courses including CS50 Introduction to Programming with Python.

title: Data and AI learning resources
content: Resources for data and AI: Kaggle Learn micro-courses for pandas, SQL and machine learning, the Machine Learning Specialization by Andrew Ng on Coursera, fast.ai practical deep learning course and the Hugging Face course for NLP.

title: Cloud and DevOps learning resources
content: Resources for cloud and DevOps: official Docker documentation, AWS Skill Builder, Microsoft Learn, KodeKloud courses and the roadmap.sh DevOps roadmap.

title: Certifications by career track
content: Well-known certifications: AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner and Microsoft Azure Fundamentals AZ-900 for cloud, Google Data Analytics Professional Certificate for data analysis, Microsoft Azure AI Fundamentals AI-900 for AI basics, CompTIA Security+ for cybersecurity, Certified Kubernetes Administrator for DevOps and Meta Front-End Developer certificate on Coursera for frontend.

title: Resume structure and length
content: Use reverse chronological order with these sections: contact info, summary, skills, experience, projects, education, certifications. Keep it to one page for students and juniors and at most two pages for experienced candidates.

title: Achievements with numbers
content: Start bullet points with strong action verbs such as built, designed, reduced or led, and add measurable results, for example: reduced page load time by 40 percent or coached 30 students in HTML and CSS. Avoid vague phrases like responsible for.

title: ATS-friendly formatting
content: Applicant tracking systems scan resumes automatically. Use standard headings, a simple single-column layout, common fonts and no text inside images or complex tables. Repeat exact keywords from the job description where they honestly apply.

title: Projects and links
content: For junior candidates, projects matter as much as experience. For each project list the tech stack, what you built, and a GitHub or live demo link. Include LinkedIn and portfolio links in the header.

title: Tailor the resume to each job
content: Adjust the summary and skills order for every application so the most relevant skills appear first. Remove old or irrelevant items, avoid buzzwords without proof and proofread for spelling mistakes.
